public_rationale: METR's March 18, 2025 preprint reports that measured task horizons doubled about every six months in its 2023–2025 model comparison using HCAST and RE-Bench, with Claude 3.7 Sonnet included (e1). This supports substantial capability progress on the evaluated tasks and contradicts the little-progress component under the contract's capability reading (e1). The study does not establish increasing returns per dollar or unit of compute (e1).
limitations: The comparison does not isolate exactly April 14, 2024–April 14, 2025 (e1).
The study reports wide error bars and sensitivity to the model period selected, limiting conclusions about the rate of progress (e1).
The evaluated tasks do not establish improvement across every application; the study also reports difficulties with messy real-world tasks (e1).
Capability gains per training dollar or unit of compute are not measured, leaving that interpretation of diminishing returns unsettled (e1).

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that frontier LLM capabilities improved little between April 2024 and publication in April 2025.
Substantial improvements in completing useful software and reasoning tasks count as doing materially more, even without reliable automation of entire jobs.
Diminishing returns could mean slowing capability gains or declining gains per unit of investment. Those meanings require different measurements.
The assessment covers the supplied capability proposition, not the separate allegation about investors' and journalists' conduct.
A substantial contradiction of the little-progress component is sufficient to contradict the combined assertion; it does not establish increasing returns to investment.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evaluations show little meaningful capability improvement over the preceding year, with declining incremental gains on a defined measure of returns.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evaluations covering models available during the preceding year show substantial improvements on meaningful tasks, contradicting the assertion that the models do little more.
